The CCEH gives its tunes as four-part scores; this page has the melody only, read from its MIDI file and checked against its incipit, and NoteFusion's engine wrote the solfa from the notes. It has not yet been checked against a printed hymn book. The arranger named above set CCEH's harmony, which is not shown here.

Questions about Ermuntre Dich Mein Schwacher

What is the doh of Ermuntre Dich Mein Schwacher?

In this version, in Eb major, doh is Eb. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Ermuntre Dich Mein Schwacher start on?

It starts on d (E♭ in Eb major), a pickup before the first full bar. Find doh first, then sing up or down to d.

What words can be sung to Ermuntre Dich Mein Schwacher?

Ermuntre Dich Mein Schwacher is in the metre 8.7.8.7.8.8.7.7: lines of 8, 7, 8, 7, 8, 8, 7, 7 syllables. Words written in the same metre fit it; check where the stresses fall before you sing them together.

Is Ermuntre Dich Mein Schwacher in the public domain?

Yes. Johann Schop died in 1664, Johann Sebastian Bach died in 1750; the tune was first published in 1641. Everyone named died before 1955 and it was published before 1929, so the tune is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements of it can still be under copyright.
